text_blocks.snippet: The first form of government in the United States was a confederation under the Articles of Confederation, which was ratified in 1781. This system established a weak central government with most powers residing with the individual states. The Articles of Confederation were ultimately replaced by the United States Constitution in 1789 due to the weaknesses of the confederation.

list.title: Weak Central Government:
list.snippet: The Articles created a system where states retained significant autonomy and the central government had limited powers, particularly in areas like taxation and regulation of commerce.

list.title: Confederation Structure:
list.snippet: The states were united in a loose alliance, rather than a strong, unified nation.

list.title: Reasons for Replacement:
list.snippet: The Articles proved inadequate as the central government lacked the authority to effectively address issues like interstate disputes, economic instability, and national defense.

list.title: Constitutional Convention (1787):
list.snippet: Recognizing the shortcomings of the Articles, delegates convened in Philadelphia to revise the document, ultimately resulting in the drafting of the United States Constitution.

list.title: United States Constitution (1789):
list.snippet: The Constitution established a stronger federal system with a balance of power between the states and the national government, replacing the Articles of Confederation.
